'''Mikhail''' "'''Mischa'''" '''Gershevich Katz''' ({{IPAc-en|k|æ|t|s}}, {{Langx|he|מיכאיל כץ}}; born 1958)<ref name="cv">[http://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~mschaps/English/Regular_Faculty/Katz_Mikhail-cv.pdf Curriculum vitae]{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, retrieved 2011-05-23.</ref> is an Israeli [[mathematician]] and professor of mathematics at [[Bar-Ilan University]]. His main interests are [[differential geometry]], [[geometric topology]], [[nonstandard analysis]], and [[mathematics education]]; he is the author of the book ''Systolic Geometry and Topology'', which is mainly about [[systolic geometry]]. The [[Katz–Sabourau inequality]] is named after him and Stéphane Sabourau.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |eprint = 1711.09963|last1 = Kalogeropoulos|first1 = Nikolaos|title = Systolic aspects of black hole entropy|class = gr-qc|year = 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Chavel |first=Isaac |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3Gjp4vQ_mPkC&pg=PA235 |title=Riemannian Geometry: A Modern Introduction |date=2006-04-10 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-139-45257-1 |language=en}}</ref>

==Biography==
Mikhail Katz was born in [[Chișinău]] in 1958. His mother was Clara Katz ([[Given name#Name at birth|née]] Landman). In 1976, he moved with his mother to the United States.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.boston.com/news/globe/obituaries/articles/2006/10/04/clara_katz_soviet_migr_saved_ailing_granddaughter/|title=Clara Katz, a Soviet émigré who saved her ailing granddaughter, dies at 85 – The Boston Globe|website=archive.boston.com|language=en|access-date=2018-01-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/news/obituaries/grandmother-bucked-the-soviet-system/2006/10/11/1160246193078.html|title=Grandmother bucked the Soviet system – Obituaries – smh.com.au|website=www.smh.com.au|date=12 October 2006|language=en|access-date=2018-01-10}}</ref>

Katz earned a bachelor's degree in 1980 from [[Harvard University]].<ref name="cv"/> He did his graduate studies at [[Columbia University]], receiving his Ph.D. in 1984 under the joint supervision of [[Troels Jørgensen]] and [[Mikhail Leonidovich Gromov|Mikhael Gromov]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=37512}}</ref> His thesis title is ''Jung's Theorem in Complex Projective Geometry.''

He moved to [[Bar-Ilan University]] in 1999, after previously holding positions at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], [[Stony Brook University]], [[Indiana University Bloomington]], the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]], the [[University of Rennes 1]], [[Henri Poincaré University]], and [[Tel Aviv University]].<ref name="cv"/>

==Work==
Katz has performed research in systolic geometry in collaboration with [[Luigi Ambrosio]], [[Victor Bangert]], [[Mikhail Gromov (mathematician)|Mikhail Gromov]], [[Steve Shnider]], [[Shmuel Weinberger]], and others. He has authored research publications appearing in journals including ''[[Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics]], [[Duke Mathematical Journal]], [[Geometric and Functional Analysis (journal)|Geometric and Functional Analysis]]'', and ''[[Journal of Differential Geometry]]''. Along with these papers, Katz was a contributor to the book "[[Metric Structures for Riemannian and Non-Riemannian Spaces]]".<ref>[[Mikhail Gromov (mathematician)|Gromov, Misha]]: ''Metric structures for Riemannian and non-Riemannian spaces''. Based on the 1981 French original. With appendices by M. Katz, P. Pansu and [[Stephen Semmes|S. Semmes]]. Translated from the French by Sean Michael Bates. Progress in Mathematics, 152. Birkhäuser Boston, Inc., Boston, MA, 1999. xx+585 pp.&nbsp;{{ISBN|0-8176-3898-9}}</ref> [[Marcel Berger]] in his article "What is... a Systole?"<ref>Berger, M.: What is... a [[systolic geometry|Systole]]? ''Notices of the AMS'' 55 (2008), no. 3, 374–376.</ref> lists Katz's 2007 book ''Systolic Geometry and Topology'' as one of two books he cites in systolic geometry.

More recently Katz also contributed to the study of [[mathematics education]], including work that provides an alternative interpretation of the number [[0.999...]].<ref>Stewart, I. (2009) ''Professor Stewart's Hoard of Mathematical Treasures'', Profile Books, p.&nbsp;174.</ref>
